method.input: native-cdp-touch; Chromium phone emulation; maximum two contacts
method.graphics: Software-WebGL fallback enabled; renderer not certified
method.inspection_note: Each action capture was viewed with view_image before adapting the next action. Driver safely paused after live captures; map planning stayed paused until CLOSE MAP. This was segmented play, not continuous human play.
method.constraints: No source, tests, docs, internal handles, earlier reviews or recordings inspected. No scripts/evaluation, keyboard, mouse, state changes, simulation advancement or server changes. Only driver help and visible UI/captures used.

outcome.terminal_note: Memories cached. Retry at the uplink with a fresh suit and a full Custodian, or start fresh.
outcome.coverage: Recovered all three memories and entered DISABLE UPLINK CUSTODIAN phase. Last live inspection showed all three coils at 100%; custodian not disabled and upload not reached. Loss occurred during active movement toward custodian, not deliberate idling. Exact lethal attack was not observed between captures.

scale.interpretation: Independent subjective scores for this single emulated portrait attempt; no target rating. Confidence limited by one attempt, segmented interaction and incomplete mission coverage.

overall_mobile.reason: A complete memory loop works in portrait with clear objectives and a useful planning map, but repeated wall-facing navigation and hard-to-track threats weakened the session.

controls.reason: Held fire, stick movement, reload, USE, scene turns and simultaneous movement/FIRE-drag registered. Many closely packed right-side buttons and repeated orientation corrections add load; fine aim remains uncertain after only one fight with drag.

gameplay.reason: Distinct receiver objectives, replenishment on recovery and armored custodian escalation give direction and stakes. Navigation dominated my attention; only one elimination and no completed boss/upload limit judgment of combat depth and balance.

presentation.reason: Cohesive rain, cyan/amber palette, industrial silhouettes, receiver fan and restrained title/debrief create a strong atmosphere at this viewport. Audio was not assessed.

usability.reason: Concise handbook, paused route map, recovery prompts, objective changes and explicit debrief support progress. Routes near cover required backtracking and the cause of sudden final damage was unclear.

readability.reason: Health/ammo, objective, memory slots and large terminal stats are legible. Compass and small threat/damage indicators are harder to parse, while close geometry can obscure nearly the whole scene.

controls_exercised: Native taps on handbook, deploy, reload, map and close map
Left stick forward/backward/strafe and direction changes
Two simultaneous contacts: movement plus held FIRE-drag aiming
Scene swipes for large and small yaw turns
Held USE for three receiver recoveries
DASH tap while moving (cooldown 0.1 visible afterward)

moments.finding: Guard centered in reticle fell to held fire; ammo 30 to 07, no health/shield loss. Clear optic/amber tutorial.
Induction structure filled scene after forward movement; had to route around it.
Map clarified a 10m receiver approach; Mara recovered while shield dropped to 22. Wall proximity made scene navigation difficult.
Initial east/north exit movement left me facing wall; map revealed position and I backed south before routing east/north. Hint was useful, but geometry-to-map translation required effort.
Moving while dragging FIRE shifted heading 000 to 352; nearby guard remained visibly alive. HOLD TO RECOVER prompt clearly identified receiver range, and Sera recovered.
2.1m CLOSER label enabled small correction; recovery completed and objective changed to custodian.

Large scene swipes turned toward route; approach was obstructed, and shield fell to 2 by 01:03. After map planning and active movement, actual loss UI appeared at 01:06. Cannot establish precise damage source or rate from these segmented captures.

missing_coverage: Physical phone performance and thermal/touch ergonomics

evidence.screenshots: All 22 JPG captures preserved; final terminal screenshot jammer-route.jpg. Two geometry requests while paused returned Not visible and no geometry was used from them.

cleanup.result: Both exact owned PIDs absent. No broad process killing.

limits: Does not establish AAA readiness or physical-device enjoyment. Single loss with pause-assisted inspection supports only the observations above. Build/source identity supplied by task, not verified by source inspection.
